c1-2-001.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: So I ___ ___ in the queue at the bakery, and this woman suddenly ___ round and hands me her dog. (stand, turn) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: So I ___ ___ in the queue at the bakery, and this woman suddenly ___ round and hands me her dog. (stand, turn)
item.why: In a story told in the present, the background is in the present continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*) and the main events in the present simple (*turns, hands*).
item.why_lv: Stāstā tagadnē fons ir Present Continuous (*I'm standing in the queue*), bet *galvenie* notikumi Present Simple (*turns, hands*).

c1-2-002.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | So this man is walking into a café and he orders a glass of milk.

key.correct: So this man is walking into a café and he orders a glass of milk.
wrong: I was waiting for the bus when suddenly this car stops right in front of me.
We're having dinner when all the lights go out.
In the film, a retired teacher moves to Lisbon and opens a café.

item.why: In a joke or a story told in the present, the main events are in the present simple: *So this man walks into a café and orders…* After a past background, a sudden event can be in the present simple (*I was waiting … when suddenly this car stops*): that is correct.
item.why_lv: Jokā vai stāstā tagadnē *galvenie* notikumi ir Present Simple: *So this* man *walks into a caf*é *and orders*… Pēc pagātnes fona pēkšņs notikums var būt Present Simple (*I was waiting* … *when suddenly this car stops*): tas ir *pareizi*.
item.correct: So this man is walking into a café and he orders a glass of milk.
wrong: I was waiting for the bus when suddenly this car stops right in front of me.
We're having dinner when all the lights go out.
In the film, a retired teacher moves to Lisbon and opens a café.

c1-2-003.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | Write one word in each gap: And Jones ___ the ball to Taylor, who ___ and scores! (pass, shoot) |

item.q: Write one word in each gap: And Jones ___ the ball to Taylor, who ___ and scores! (pass, shoot)
item.why: In a live commentary, quick actions that are over as you speak are in the present simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* would describe a longer action in progress.
item.why_lv: Tiešraides komentārā ātras darbības, kas beidzas runāšanas brīdī, ir Present Simple: *passes, shoots, scores*. *is passing* aprakstītu ilgāku darbību, kas vēl notiek.

c1-2-004.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I'm gathering you're looking for a new flat.

key.correct: I'm gathering you're looking for a new flat.
wrong: I hear the bridge will be closed all summer.
Anna tells me you've started running.
It says here the museum is free on Sundays.

item.why: To pass on news we have heard or read, we use the present simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here*. Not *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*
item.why_lv: Lai *nodotu* dzirdētu vai izlasītu ziņu, lieto Present Simple: *I gather, I hear, Anna tells me, It says here.* Nevis *I'm gathering*: *I gather you're looking for a new flat.*
item.correct: I'm gathering you're looking for a new flat.
wrong: I hear the bridge will be closed all summer.
Anna tells me you've started running.
It says here the museum is free on Sundays.

c1-2-005.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I'm wondering could you look at my CV before Friday.

key.correct: I'm wondering could you look at my CV before Friday.
wrong: We're hoping to move in by the end of May.
I was wondering if you were free on Thursday.
I wonder whether you'd mind helping me with this.

item.why: After *I'm wondering*, the question becomes *if / whether* + statement order: *I'm wondering whether you could look at my CV.*
item.why_lv: Aiz *I'm wondering* jautājums kļūst par *if / whether + apgalvojuma* vārdu secību: *I'm wondering whether you could look at my CV.*
item.correct: I'm wondering could you look at my CV before Friday.
wrong: We're hoping to move in by the end of May.
I was wondering if you were free on Thursday.
I wonder whether you'd mind helping me with this.

c1-2-006.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | order | Put the words in order. | I'm wondering whether you could help me with this

key.sentence: I'm wondering whether you could help me with this

item.why: A polite request: *I'm wondering whether* + statement order (*you could*), not question order (*could you*).
item.why_lv: Pieklājīgs lūgums: *I'm wondering whether + apgalvojuma* vārdu secība (*you could*), nevis jautājuma secība (*could you*).
item.sentence: I'm wondering whether you could help me with this
answers: I'm wondering whether you could help me with this

c1-2-007.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | The app ___ to work on my phone. Can you check it? (not / appear) |

item.q: The app ___ to work on my phone. Can you check it? (not / appear)
item.why: *appear* = seem is a state: present simple, *doesn't appear to work*. In the meaning *take part* it can be continuous (*She's appearing in a musical*).
item.why_lv: *appear* = šķist ir stāvoklis: Present Simple, *doesn't appear to work*. Nozīmē piedalīties, uzstāties var būt Continuous forma (*She's appearing in a musical*).

c1-2-008.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | gap | My sister and her husband ___ their first baby in June. (expect) |

item.q: My sister and her husband ___ their first baby in June. (expect)
item.why: *be expecting a baby* = she is pregnant, always continuous. In the meaning *think something will happen*, *expect* is simple (*I expect it will rain*).
item.why_lv: *be expecting a baby = gaida* bērnu, vienmēr Continuous forma. Nozīmē domāt, ka kaut kas notiks *expect* ir vienkāršajā formā (*I expect it will rain*).

c1-2-009.gate_key: adv_present | C1 | mcq | Which sentence has a mistake? | I'm promising I'll pay you back on Friday.

key.correct: I'm promising I'll pay you back on Friday.
wrong: I suggest we meet at the station.
We regret that the flight has been cancelled.
I'm not suggesting you were careless.

item.why: When saying the words is the act itself (promising, suggesting, regretting), use the present simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.* In the negative, *I'm not suggesting* is also correct.
item.why_lv: Ja paši vārdi ir darbība (apsolīt, *ieteikt*, izteikt nožēlu), lieto Present Simple: *I promise I'll pay you back.* Noliegumā *pareizi* ir arī *I'm not suggesting.*
item.correct: I'm promising I'll pay you back on Friday.
wrong: I suggest we meet at the station.
We regret that the flight has been cancelled.
I'm not suggesting you were careless.
